text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Main workers' Union Generale des Travailleurs Algeriens (UGTA) threatens action after failure of negociations with government officials over salary increase.
- Parliamentary election watchdog committee head Salah Boubnider to hold news conference on April 7.
- Algeria may reach an association accord with the European Union in October.

- Information and justice ministries' representatives withdraw from election watchdog and are replaced by opposition party officials in order to keep the authorities neutral as promised by President Liamine Zeroual.
- Political stability in Algeria will lead to improvement in the security situation, says senior European Union official.
- U.S.-based Human Rights Watch representatives meet officials from Algerian multi-party election committee over the June 5 legislative election preparations.
- Interior Minister Mustapha Ben Mansour said the authorities would be neutral to ensure a fair and free elections.
- Inflation rate falls to 10 percent from 40 percent.
- French parliament member and former security chief Yves Bonnet says the situation in Algeria has improved.
